findings.what: A stopped watcher can remove its replacement's registration. Start watcher A for a delivered conversation, stop it while a read/sleep is pending, then recover the same conversation successfully and start B. Both registrations use the identical key/agent string. When A eventually settles, its finally deletes B's entry. The next GET therefore stops B and starts another recovered watcher, re-baselining reviews that arrived while B was pending and potentially treating an unprocessed change as already attended. Use a unique registration object or promise per start and compare that identity before cleanup. Test delayed settlement of A after B starts with the real ReviewWatch; the current double replaces the settlement resolver by agent and cannot exercise this ordering.

These compare a reusable conversation key, not the particular registration. ReviewWatch itself uses live.get(key) === attended at review-watch.ts:179; the new outer cleanup does not retain that identity.
